engine: Fresh isolated PGlite databases; no Forge data accessed

probes.setup: CREATE TABLE parent(code text UNIQUE); CREATE TABLE child(code text REFERENCES parent(code));
probes.query: INSERT INTO parent VALUES ('a'); INSERT INTO child VALUES ('a'); SELECT code FROM child;
probes.claim: A foreign key is not restricted to referencing a primary key; an appropriate UNIQUE key is valid.

probes.setup: CREATE TABLE people(id int PRIMARY KEY,name text); INSERT INTO people VALUES(1,'Ada'),(2,'Lin');
probes.query: SELECT id,name,count(*)::int AS n FROM people GROUP BY id ORDER BY id;
probes.claim: PostgreSQL allows selecting columns functionally dependent on a grouped primary key.

probes.setup: CREATE TABLE a(id int); CREATE TABLE b(id int);
probes.claim: Plain JOIN without ON/USING/NATURAL is a syntax error, not an implicit Cartesian product.
probes.error: error: syntax error at or near ";"

probes.setup: CREATE TABLE bag(value int); INSERT INTO bag VALUES(1),(1);
probes.query: SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM bag;
probes.claim: SQL tables can contain duplicate rows unless constraints remove that possibility.

probes.query: SELECT (SELECT 1 WHERE false) IS NULL AS is_null;
probes.claim: A scalar subquery may return zero rows, producing NULL; it need not return exactly one row.

probes.query: EXPLAIN WITH q AS (SELECT generate_series(1,2) AS n) SELECT a.n FROM q a JOIN q b ON a.n=b.n;
probes.claim: A multiply referenced side-effect-free CTE can be materialized by default; not all PostgreSQL 12+ CTEs are automatically inlined.

->  CTE Scan on q b  (cost=0.00..0.04 rows=2 width=4)

probes.setup: CREATE TABLE ident(id int GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY); INSERT INTO ident VALUES(1);
probes.claim: An explicit value in a BY DEFAULT identity column does not automatically advance its sequence; identity does not prevent every desynchronization.
probes.error: error: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ident_pkey"
